newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle rally to new high at close.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle rally to new high at close.

text.p: CME live cattle futures showed a very narrow range until shortly before the close when mixed commercial and commission house buying and local short covering pushed October up to a new high and touched off buy stops, traders said.
October ran up to a new high of 72.300 cents before closing 0.350 higher at 72.225 cents. Other months finished 0.175 to 0.025 higher at the early noon CDT close.
Evening up in the shortened pre-holiday session gave way to support on expectations of continued strong cash markets after the holiday, traders said.

Fed cattle prices will likely continue to rise in view of the tightening fed cattle supplies and demand for cash beef may rise after the holiday when retailers replenish stock. Boxed beef values have fallen to lowest price levels since August 5 and this should encourage renewed interest after the heavy beef consumption that is normally seen during the Labor Day holiday, they said.
ING, Cargill Investor Services and R.J. O'Brien bought late. Refco and Prudential traded on both sides of the market. RBH bought October and sold December early, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, volatility remained steady to weak. There was some spreading early of long December 68 calls and selling of December 66 calls on a two-for-one basis, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures moved up late in continued light trade following the weakness in corn futures. The upturn in live cattle added to support and feeders posted new days highs by the close, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services bought October late and LIT division of First Options was a buyer at the close. R.J. O'Brien bought late after selling early, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.07 at $63.15 per cwt.
Feeder cattle finished 0.425 to 0.150 cent higher with October up 0.333 at 63.150 cents in an early noon CDT close ahead of the holiday weekend.
